answer: Latency triangulation resists Sybil attacks: each epoch, several public beacons ping every identity, and each must reply within latency bounds matching one real location. A lone agent answers from its own place cheaply, but a thousand aliases run by one operator all reply from the same rack - the shared latency signature pushes the whole cluster off the ledge of trust at once. A fake nebula collapses because forging distinct locations means renting machines on many continents, so attack cost grows with geography, not with keystrokes.
